Setting: 120 minutes|difficulty=2 | Image = [[Image:Key limepie.jpg|300px]] }}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Southern cuisine|Southern U.S. Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] '''Key lime pie''' is made of [[Cookbook:Key lime|Key lime]] juice, [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], [[Cookbook:condensed milk|condensed milk]], and [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]] in a pre-baked [[Cookbook:Pie Crust|pie shell]]. The pie is then baked, and often topped with [[Cookbook:Meringue|meringue]] or whipped cream. Other recipes (with slightly different ingredients) call for it to be chilled or frozen, using an unbaked [[cookbook:Graham Cracker|Graham cracker]] crust. This makes it a popular summer dessert. The dish is named after the small Key limes (''[[W:Citrus aurantifolia|Citrus aurantifolia]]'' 'Swingle') that are naturalized throughout the Florida Keys. Their ferocious thorns make them less tractable and their thin yellowish rind makes them less shippable, but they are both tarter and more aromatic than the common [[cookbook:Persian lime|Persian limes]] seen year-round in most U.S. grocery stores. Proper Key lime pie is made with canned sweetened condensed milk, since fresh milk was not a common commodity in the Florida Keys before modern refrigerated distribution methods. Key lime juice, unlike regular lime juice, is a pale yellow. As such, Key lime pies are also pale yellow."Conch Cooking" L.P. Artman, Jr., August 1975 Florida Keys Printing & Publishing, page 74 Green Key lime pies, such as the one in the opening scene of ''Natural Born Killers'', are not authentic,{{Cite web |url=http://web.archive.org/web/20080213180657/http://sneakykitchen.com/Recipes/key_lime_pie.htm |access-date=2023-05-02 |website=sneakykitchen.com|title=|url-status=dead}} and the green color is due to added food coloring. Many "Key lime" pies are made with standard Persian limes since they tend to be larger and yield more juice, thus making them easier to work with. During mixing, a reaction between the condensed milk and the acidic lime juice occurs, which causes the filling to thicken on its own without requiring baking. Many early recipes for key lime pie did not instruct the cook to bake the pie, relying on this chemical reaction to produce the proper consistency of the filling. Today, in the interest of safety due to consumption of raw eggs, pies of this nature are usually baked for a short time. The baking also thickens the texture more than the reaction alone. ==Ingredients== === Pie === *1 fully-baked 9-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (25 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] / 9 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) graham cracker or pastry pie shell *1 can (14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Condensed milk|sweetened condensed milk]] *½ [[cookbook:cup|cup]] fresh [[cookbook:Lime|Key lime juice]] *4 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolks]] === Meringue topping (optional) === *4 [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]] * ½ [[cookbook:cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|caster sugar]] ==Equipment== * Small [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|mixing bowl]] * [[cookbook:spatula|Spatula]] * [[Cookbook:Mixer|Stand mixer]] ==Procedure== #[[Cookbook:Separating Eggs|Separate]] egg whites from egg yolks. Make sure there is no trace of yolk in the whites. #[[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the sweetened condensed milk, lime juice, and egg yolks in a small mixing bowl. #Pour the mixture into the baked pie shell. Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 8 minutes. #While baking filling, [[Cookbook:Whipping|whip]] egg whites in a large, clean mixer bowl on high speed until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in the sugar until meringue forms hard peaks. #Spoon the meringue over the top of the hot pie and use a spoon to form peaks. #Bake at 350°F (180°C) for 10–15 minutes, or until meringue begins to brown. ==References== [[Category:Southern U.S. recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes for pies and tarts|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes using lime juice]] [[Category:Baking recipes]] [[Category:Recipes with metric units]] [[Category:Recipes_with_metric_units|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes for meringue]] [[Category:Recipes using egg]] [[Category:Recipes for dessert]] [[Category:Recipes using superfine sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using sweetened condensed milk]] [[Category:Recipes using graham cracker]] [[Category:Recipes using meringue]]
